one_line: A Galei Tzahal (גלי צה"ל) radio-station Reel, shot in its studio with a guest parenting expert named in the caption, where the hosts voice six blunt child questions (where babies come from, why daycare, where grandpa is, two dads, parents fighting, sirens) and the guest gives short age-aware answers under big Hebrew captions.

hook.visual: Close-up of a woman with a grey ponytail, glasses and black turtleneck mid-answer, radio mic and monitor in frame, station logo top right; hard cut at 0:02 to a blonde host in an orange striped top and headphones.
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: It opens on the blunt answer to a taboo question before any question is shown (observed 0:00 caption, matches transcript), so the viewer has to keep watching to learn what was asked. At 0:02 the caption 'לו הייתי סופר נני' (If I were Super Nanny) and the post caption 'מה סופר נני הייתה עונה??' turn it into a game of 'what would the expert say'.

beats.observed: Expert close-up, hand gesture, burned-in white caption over the lower third.
Cut to the blonde host (0:02), then to a dark-haired host in a yellow top (0:04); the child question is in yellow with quote marks.
beats.spoken: לוא, הייתי סופר נני. אימא, איך באים לעולם? (If I were Super Nanny. Mom, how do people come into the world?)
beats.on_screen_text: לו הייתי סופר נני (If I were Super Nanny) / "אמא איך באים לעולם?" ("Mom, how do people come into the world?")

beats.observed: Expert answers with big hand gestures, three caption chunks of 2-4 words each.
beats.spoken: A couple who love each other very much hug and out of love decide to make a child; then 'good for age three', 'good for age four', 'at seven or eight more than this'.
beats.on_screen_text: כשזוג מאוד מאוד אוהב / מתחבקים ומתוך אהבה / זה מעולה לגיל שלוש / זה מעולה לגיל ארבע / בגיל שבע שמונה יותר מזה (When a couple loves very much / hug and out of love / this is great for age three / great for age four / at age seven eight, more than this)

beats.observed: Blonde host asks the next child question; expert answers; a bearded host in headphones appears at 0:20 with a yellow quoted line.
beats.spoken: Mom, why do we have to go to daycare? Children are not left alone at home, someone has to take care of them. (host as child) My mom? Yes.
beats.on_screen_text: "אמא למה צריך ללכת לגן?" ("Mom, why do we have to go to daycare?") / לא משאירים ילדים לבד בבית (We do not leave children alone at home) / "אמא שלי" ("My mom")

beats.observed: Bearded host asks where grandpa is; the hook line returns; a host asks at what age she says it; expert answers with a fist gesture and a laugh.
beats.spoken: Where is grandpa? Grandpa died, sweetie. At what age do you say 'grandpa died'? From the moment he is born. Precisely because they are small you can tell them the truth, since they do not understand the meaning.
beats.on_screen_text: "איפה סבא?" ("Where is grandpa?") / באיזה גיל את אומרת לו סבא מת? (At what age do you tell him grandpa died?) / מהרגע שהוא נולד (From the moment he is born) / דווקא בגלל שהם קטנים (Precisely because they are small) / אפשר להגיד להם את האמת (You can tell them the truth) / מבינים את המשמעות (understand the meaning; the frame at 0:32 shows no 'לא' before it, while the transcript has 'לא מבינים')

beats.observed: Dark-haired host reads the next child question; expert answers leaning on her hand, with short caption chunks; the question is about two dads.
beats.spoken: Why does Tali have two dads? Because they love each other very much and wanted to be a couple and wanted to be Tali's parents. Today you do not have to have a mom and a dad: two dads, and also two moms.
beats.on_screen_text: "למה לטלי יש שני אבות?" ("Why does Tali have two dads?") / כי הם מאוד אוהבים אחד את השני (Because they love each other very much) / והם רצו להיות ההורים של טלי (and they wanted to be Tali's parents) / לא חייבים שיהיה אמא ואבא (you do not have to have a mom and dad) / אפשר שני אבות (two dads are possible) / אפשר גם שתי אמהות (two moms are also possible)

beats.observed: Blonde host asks why parents fight; expert gives a direct-address example to an imagined child about fighting with a friend in first grade; cutaway to the blonde host listening (1:02) while the expert's line continues.
beats.spoken: Why do mom and dad (or mom and mom, or dad and dad) fight all the time? Because they disagree about a lot of things. Remember how you fought in first grade, or kindergarten, and then you became friends again and play with him again? When people sometimes disagree.
beats.on_screen_text: "רבים כל הזמן?" ("fight all the time?") / כי הם לא מסכימים על המון דברים (because they disagree about many things) / אתה זוכר (do you remember) / איך רבת כשהיית בכיתה א' (how you fought in first grade) / אבל אחר כך חזרתם להיות חברים (but afterwards you became friends again) / כי אנשים לפעמים לא מסכימים (because people sometimes disagree)

beats.observed: Heaviest topic: expert's voice continues over cutaways to the bearded host's serious face (1:16); the question itself was not captured in a sampled frame.
beats.spoken: Why is there a siren/alert? [Whisper: 'למה יש הזקה', probably 'אזעקה', inferred] Because we have enemies; enemies are people who do not like that we are here and have a silly idea that they will succeed in driving us away; so they scare us, and the alert is so that we are in a safe place.
beats.on_screen_text: כי יש לנו אויבים (because we have enemies) / אויבים זה אנשים שלא אוהבים (enemies are people who do not like) / שאנחנו פה (that we are here) / שהם יצליחו לגרש אותנו מפה (that they will succeed in driving us out of here) / אז הם מפחידים אותנו (so they scare us) / כדי שנהיה (so that we will be)

beats.observed: Release beat: the dark-haired host smiles and says she calmed down (yellow captions with dash and quote marks), then the blonde host laughs at 1:24 with no caption.
beats.spoken: 'I calmed down' repeated three times; then 'What is this? That was a real Olympics?' [last sentence low reliability, Whisper 'אולימפיאדת'].
beats.on_screen_text: נרגעתי (I calmed down) + second line partly legible, reads like גבירותיי at 1:20 and רבותיי at 1:22 (ladies / gentlemen), exact punctuation [unclear]

payoff: Immediate and repeated: the first answer lands at 0:00, the age-tiered 'love and hugs' answer at 0:04-0:15, then a new question and answer every 10-18 s through 1:19. The emotional release (hosts laughing 'נרגעתי') is the closing payoff at 1:19-1:24.
cta: Caption only: "מה אתם הייתם שואלים אותה?" (What would you ask her?) and a pointer to the full episode on all platforms. No spoken or on-screen CTA inside the 86 s.
share_or_comment_trigger: Parents recognise the awkward child questions and want to save or send the expert's exact wording (for example how to tell a young child a grandparent died); the caption invites a 'what would you ask her' comment. Only 97 comments against 5,908 likes, so a soft open question drove few comments; shares and saves are not in meta.
why_it_worked: Cold open on the blunt answer (0:00) plus the 'Super Nanny' framing at 0:02 creates a curiosity gap in the first 2 s (observed caption, inferred effect).
Six self-contained question and answer units in 86 s, a cut every 2-5 s between three or four studio angles, and 2-4 word burned-in captions give a payoff every 10-15 s (observed in frames).

132,761 views is 4.0x the expert account's 33,600 median with a 4.45% like rate, too high to look like paid promotion; the radio station's own audience through the collab post is the likely extra reach (inferred, station follower count not in meta).
paid_signal: no: like_rate_pct 4.45 is far above the 0.3 paid-promotion flag and outlier_x is a modest 4.0, so it reads as an organic collab post; boosting cannot be ruled out from meta alone.

solo_route.how: 1. List 5-6 blunt questions kids ask at ages 3-8 (from LumeBook DMs, parent-group posts, comments), each written in a short child voice, for example "איפה סבא?". 2. Barter a child-development expert (the existing barter route) for a 15-minute seated recording with the social media manager as host voicing the kid questions; film on two phones at 9:16 from two angles with two cheap lav mics. 3. In CapCut: cold-open on the single bluntest answer line in the first second, then the question; Hebrew auto-captions in 2-4 word chunks (yellow for host/child voice, white for the expert); cut between angles every 2-5 s and add reaction cutaways; keep each Q&A under 15 s. 4. Close on a laugh or release line and ask in the caption what question the child asked this week.
solo_route.needs: A barter expert who consents to be filmed and posted; a second person is optional because the social media manager can host; no child on camera is needed. Keep advice strictly to what the expert actually says.

lumebook_version.hook_he: ילד בן 4 שואל "מאיפה באים תינוקות?" מה עונים לו?
lumebook_version.concept: A rapid-fire 'what would the expert answer' Reel: five age-tagged questions from kids 3-8 (new sibling, why preschool, where babies come from), a barter child-development expert answers each in under 12 s with the age band on screen, opening on the bluntest answer. The end card shows a LumeBook page with the child as the hero of a story about the same big question.

evidence_notes: Observed: all 8 sheets (0:00-1:24, frame every 2 s) and single frames at 0:02, 0:32, 1:20, 1:22, 1:24. Speaker roles are inferred from camera cuts and caption colour: yellow captions are mostly the hosts' lines and child questions in quotes, white is mostly the expert's answers (exception: the white 'לו הייתי סופר נני' at 0:02 is a host line). The woman answering all questions is inferred to be the guest named in the caption (מיכל דליות); that is not confirmed by any on-screen name. Hosts are not named in frames. who made it: the post owner in meta is the radio station (גלי צה"ל glz) and the caption says the guest 'התארחה אצלנו באולפן' with the full episode 'מחכה לכם בכל הפלטפורמות', plus the station's show logo (גלצ, טוב שבאתם) is burned into every frame, so I read it as a station in-house edit with an expert guest, not a creator collab edit and not expert self-posted; meta 'account' (michal_dalyot) is the collab co-author, so outlier_x and the 33,600 median are the expert account's, not the station's. Whisper Hebrew is mostly coherent and matches captions; weak spots: 1:06.9 'למה יש הזקה' (likely אזעקה, inferred; the question was not in a sampled frame), 1:22 'אולימפיאדת' (low confidence), 'נישהו' (probably מישהו), 'לא מבינים' versus the 0:32 caption without 'לא'. No kids appear on screen. Music and tone not assessed.
